memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then he brought Aaron's sons forward, put tunics on them, tied sashes around them and fastened caps on them, as the LORD commanded Moses." - Lev 8:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Aaron's sons receive simpler garments than their father — tunics, sashes, caps. No ephod, no breastpiece, no gold plate. Their role was real but different.

And they too are dressed by Moses. The same passive posture, the same received qualification.

There is a lesson here about different callings within one household of faith. The sons were not lesser priests; they were priests with a different function. Israel needed both the one who entered the Most Holy Place and the many who tended the altar daily.

Paul develops this at length: There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit... Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it (1 Cor 12:4, 27). He specifically addresses the person who feels their role is insignificant: If the foot should say, "Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body," it would not for that reason stop being part of the body (1 Cor 12:15).

Comparison is a persistent thief in church life. We look at the visible ministries and quietly conclude our own contribution barely counts.

The tunic was as much a priestly garment as the ephod. Wear yours.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I compare my role in God's work unfavourably with someone else's?
2. What has God actually given me to do, and am I doing it faithfully?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the place You have given me in Your work. Keep me from comparison, and help me serve faithfully in my own calling. Amen.
